title: Zone risk ranking by incident frequency
sql: ORDER BY COUNT(i.incident_id) DESC) AS risk_rank
LEFT JOIN incident i ON i.zone_id = z.zone_id

steps.title: Left join incidents
steps.text: Zones are the preserved side. North Zone matches incidents 1, 3 and 4, and South Zone matches incidents 2 and 5. A zone with no incidents would still appear.

steps.title: Count per zone
steps.text: COUNT(i.incident_id) ignores NULLs, giving 3 for North Zone and 2 for South Zone.

steps.title: Rank the groups
steps.text: The window runs after grouping. DENSE_RANK gives equal counts the same rank and leaves no gaps, so the busiest zone is rank 1.

title: Top species in human-wildlife conflicts
sql: JOIN animal a ON a.animal_id = hwc.animal_id
JOIN species sp ON sp.species_id = a.species_id

steps.title: Join conflicts to animals
steps.text: All four conflicts have an animal. Conflicts 1 and 2 point to animal 1, conflict 3 to animal 3 and conflict 4 to animal 4. Rows with a NULL animal_id would be dropped by the inner join.

steps.title: Resolve species
steps.text: Animals 1 and 4 are leopards and animal 3 is a tiger. The sloth bear has no conflicts and never appears.

steps.title: Count and rank
steps.text: Leopards have 3 conflicts and tigers 1. The result is sorted by count and capped by LIMIT.

title: Habitual conflict animals
sql: JOIN species sp ON sp.species_id = a.species_id
JOIN human_wildlife_conflict hwc ON hwc.animal_id = a.animal_id

steps.title: Join animals to conflicts
steps.text: Animals without a conflict, such as animal 2, drop out of the inner join.

steps.title: Group and count
steps.text: Animal 1 has 2 conflicts. Animals 3 and 4 have 1 each.

steps.title: Filter groups with HAVING
steps.text: WHERE cannot see aggregates, so HAVING keeps only groups with at least 2 conflicts. Animals 3 and 4 are rejected.

title: Incident severity by species threat level
sql: JOIN animal a ON a.species_id = sp.species_id
JOIN human_wildlife_conflict hwc ON hwc.animal_id = a.animal_id
JOIN incident i ON i.incident_id = hwc.incident_id

steps.title: Chain the joins
steps.text: Species lead to animals, then to conflicts, then to incidents. The sloth bear has no conflicts and drops out. Incident 2 has no conflict and is never reached.

steps.title: Group by threat level
steps.text: Leopards are vulnerable and own incidents 1, 3 and 4. The tiger is endangered and owns incident 5.

steps.title: Count critical incidents
steps.text: FILTER counts only critical incidents. Incident 3 is critical, so vulnerable has 1 of 3 and endangered has 0 of 1.

steps.title: Compute the ratio
steps.text: NULLIF guards the division, and the result is a percentage rounded to two decimals.

title: Endangered sighting density per square kilometer
sql: JOIN sighting s ON s.zone_id = z.zone_id
JOIN animal a ON a.animal_id = s.animal_id
JOIN species sp ON sp.species_id = a.species_id

steps.title: Join sightings to species
steps.text: Each sighting is matched to its zone, then to its animal and species.

steps.title: Keep threatened species
steps.text: Leopards and sloth bears are vulnerable and tigers are endangered, so every sighting passes the threat filter.

steps.title: Count per zone
steps.text: North Zone has 4 sightings and South Zone has 2. The area is measured with ST_Area on the geography boundary.

steps.title: Divide by area
steps.text: NULLIF turns a zero area into NULL instead of a division error. Zones are sorted by density.

steps.title: Reduce to reporter months
steps.text: The CTE keeps one row per reporter and month: user 2 in September and October, user 1 in October and November, and user 3 in November.

steps.title: Self join the prior month
steps.text: The CTE is joined to itself. A reporter matches the earlier copy only if they were also active exactly one month before. LEFT JOIN keeps reporters with no match.

steps.title: Count per month
steps.text: September has 1 active reporter and none retained. October has 2 active and 1 retained (user 2). November has 2 active and 1 retained (user 1).
